evidence.summary: cancel(order) sets status to 'cancelled' whatever the current status; its comment says a paid order is cancelled without a refund
The user describes Orderly as orders with states pending, paid, cancelled, refunded

features.name: Order lifecycle states
features.description: Orders carry one of four states: pending, paid, cancelled, refunded
features.observed_behaviour: The states are declared; no code sets 'paid' or 'refunded' and no transition table exists
features.business_logic: Allowed values: pending, paid, cancelled, refunded. Transitions are not defined in the code.

features.name: Cancel an order
features.observed_behaviour: cancel() overwrites status with 'cancelled' for any order, including paid and refunded ones
features.business_logic: No refund for a paid order; no guard against cancelling twice or cancelling a refunded order.

entities.name: Order
entities.description: An order as Orderly sees it: something with a lifecycle status (an in-memory dict)

architecture.backend: one function and a states tuple

unknowns: How orders are created, stored and looked up: no code for it
Which code moves an order to paid or refunded: none in Orderly
Rights: task.md states no rights and there is no licence file, so code_reuse is unknown and nothing is copied
